building.completed_conflict: This address is recorded as built 1883; the assessor's roll gives 1910, the year it files most of the city's nineteenth-century buildings under.

historical_record.description: Built by Charles L. Hinkel, whose family firm was among the Bay Area's leading residential builders in the late nineteenth century; his work is marked by canted narrow windows with keystone lintels, pedimented gables with boxed eaves and prominent scrolled brackets.
